name: SparkRx
one_liner: Five-week, self-guided CBT app for teens and young adults with depression symptoms, used alongside care from a clinician.
best_for: Teens and young adults (about 13-22) with depression symptoms who are already seeing a clinician
Families whose health plan, employer or clinician offers SparkRx
Young people who want to practise CBT skills like behavioral activation between appointments
not_for: Anyone in crisis: call or text 988
Young people with severe depression who need more intensive care
People without access through a clinician, employer or health plan (no direct purchase found)
short_description: A five-week self-guided CBT program app for teens and young adults with depression, used with a clinician's care. Owned by Big Health.
long_description: SparkRx was made by Limbix, which Big Health bought in July 2023. It is a five-week, self-guided program based on cognitive behavioral therapy and behavioral activation, teaching skills such as mood tracking, planning rewarding activities, problem solving and mindfulness. It is meant as an add-on to care from a clinician and is offered through clinicians, employers, health systems and health plans; it is not FDA-cleared and was marketed under FDA's pandemic-era enforcement discretion. In a 2023 published feasibility trial (60 adolescents), depression symptoms fell in both SparkRx and a control app, with no significant difference between them. Limbix reported larger phase II results in 2021 only in press releases and a conference poster, where the main comparison with the control app was not statistically significant; results of its registered efficacy trial were not found. Its current availability was not confirmed.
patient_summary: SparkRx is a phone program for teens and young adults with depression that teaches CBT skills over five weeks, on top of seeing a clinician. You get it through a clinician, health plan or employer that offers Big Health's programs; we found no way to buy it yourself.

pricing.starting_price: Through a clinician, employer or health plan; contact Big Health
pricing.notes: No published consumer price. Big Health offers it through employers, health systems, public sector and health plan customers and pharmacy benefit agreements.

privacy.notes: Big Health privacy notice (read 2026-10-27) says it may 'sell' or 'share' data via advertising cookies and pixels on its corporate website and lets ad partners collect identifiers and activity data for interest-based ads; deletion requests offered to all users regardless of location.

seo.title: SparkRx: Digital Therapeutic for Teen Depression | HeyPsych
seo.meta_description: SparkRx is the first digital therapeutic for adolescents ages 13-22 with depression symptoms. Self-guided CBT and behavioral activation through mobile app.

faqs.a: SparkRx is a digital therapeutic designed for adolescents and young adults ages 13-22 with symptoms of depression, delivering self-guided CBT and behavioral activation through a mobile app.
SparkRx is not FDA cleared but was made available under the FDA's COVID-19 enforcement policy for psychiatric digital health devices. Big Health acquired Limbix, the creator of SparkRx, in 2023.
Clinical trials showed a 21% remission rate compared to 4% for control groups, with treatment response rates of 29% versus 16% for SparkRx users.
Big Health, the company behind SleepioRx and DaylightRx, acquired Limbix in 2023 to expand into adolescent mental health.

clinical_trials.study: Spark (SparkRx) vs an active control app as an add-on treatment for adolescents with depression symptoms

citation.title: A CBT-based mobile intervention as an adjunct treatment for adolescents with symptoms of depression: a virtual randomized controlled feasibility trial

clinical_trials.outcome: Feasible and acceptable; depression symptoms fell in both groups with no significant difference between Spark and the control app. Authors were from Limbix.
clinical_trials.study_design: Randomized controlled feasibility trial (active control app)

availability.note: Only through clinicians, employers, health systems or health plans that offer Big Health programs; no direct purchase found. Current status in 2026 not confirmed.
